name: Ersveil (open world)
author: Story Suite examples
description: The world of Ersveil as an open world pack: lore, a map of 323 places joined by routes, 31 people (12 companions and 19 world figures), 22 realms, 15 powers and 4 world scores, 31 conditions, the world events of eleven threads and the templates the Director may draw on. It lists no items, shops, prices or foes: the story makes them up from the lore. A new story begins at the Adventurer Guild office in Bluewatch Village on 1 October CY 611.

places.name: Highmark Capital
places.note: Imperial throne city of walled districts; seals, legal services and arms contracts.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Crown Keep
places.note: Palace, Diet and War Office; imperial warrants and sealed petitions.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Noble Heights
places.note: Walled noble estates: tailors, fine tack, household retainers.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Knight Quarter
places.note: Barracks and tilting yards; arms repair, cavalry tack, officer lodging.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Civic Ward
places.note: Tax courts, guildhalls and tenements; daily provisions and common lodging.

places.name: Iron Guard Fortress
places.note: Main imperial stronghold; armour repair and siege stores.

places.name: Barak Freeport
places.note: Highmark's southern port at the head of the Barak Gulf; Belis River freight lands here.

places.name: Oathmere
places.note: Highmark lake town of horse breeders and fishers (the lake of the same name lies beside it).

places.name: Stoneford
places.note: Fortified road town on the way to Barak; wagon repair, base for the Southmarch Road.

places.name: Ravenholt
places.note: Western border fortress at the head of the Barrens caravan road; raider watch.

places.name: Thornwall Redoubt
places.note: The Wardens of the Last Wall's fortress on Highmark's northern march, where the roads from the Border Kingdoms and Valegard meet; the Last Wall's earthworks run east and west from it.

places.name: Thousand Sails
places.note: River Council seat and fleet hub; bulk cargo and contract brokers.

places.name: Thousand Sails / Council Quay
places.note: River Council chambers and toll courts; charters and contract witnesses.

places.name: Thousand Sails / Grand Bazaar
places.note: Wholesale market and warehouses; bulk imports and foreign merchant courts.

places.name: Thousand Sails / Hulkrow
places.note: Old barges moored together as floating slums for the poor and those in hiding.

places.name: Ledgerford
places.note: Banking city: assay, deposits, bank notes, sealed contracts.

places.name: Ledgerford / Vault Row
places.note: The great banks behind armed vaults.

places.name: Ledgerford / Assay Hall
places.note: Every coin weighed, every note honoured or refused.

places.name: Ledgerford / Debtors' Steps
places.note: Public auctions of debts, collateral and bondfolk.

places.name: Bluewatch Village
places.note: Northernmost village: river watchpoint, Auvoth convoy supplies, cold-weather gear.

places.name: Bluewatch Village / Guild Office
places.note: Adventurer Guild branch desk where new arrivals register and read the job board.

places.name: Mirage City
places.note: Pleasure city of theatres, auctions and gambling credit.

places.name: Coinwater
places.note: Confederacy mint city; coin assay and sealed freight receipts.

places.name: Saltledger Quay
places.note: Estuary port: salt, fish, sea-river customs and pilot contracts.

places.name: Glassdock
places.note: Port for fragile cargo where the Bluewatch Branch meets the Glassdock Channel.

places.name: Lowmarket Reach
places.note: Caravan entry to Confederacy markets; freight transfer and Mirage-road guides.

places.name: Floodbell
places.note: Floodgate town: levee tools, emergency grain; second approach to Drowned Bell Vault.

places.name: Brightwater Lock
places.note: Fortified customs lock on the northern Ledger; gateway to Chainlock Depths.

places.name: Ferrywake
places.note: Ferry-chain town; start of the causeway to Drowned Bell Vault.

places.name: Marshledger
places.note: Estuary accounting town: salt and fish accounts, pilot contracts.

places.name: Shorn
places.note: Ducal capital and Confederacy bastion on the road to Auvoth.

places.name: Old Lantern Post
places.note: Shrine-town at the edge of settled land; lamp oil, trail blessings, wayfarer shelter.

places.name: Hearthmere
places.note: Hot-spring refuge town with bathhouses, winter lodging and reserve granaries.

places.name: Greyvein Camp
places.note: Mining camp and gateway to the Rimeglass Galleries; cold iron, blue coal, dungeon permits.

places.name: Frostgate
places.note: Last lock before Shorn and head of navigation; sledges beyond.

places.name: Rimebridge
places.note: Toll fortress tying Shornmarch to Ledgerford; convoy papers, guarded warehousing.

places.name: Wolfmere Outpost
places.note: Scout post on the Auvoth bastion road; reports, remounts, escort hire.

places.name: Hollin's Reach
places.note: Northernmost Shornmarch village; wool, mutton and hay by barter, little coin.

places.name: Auvoth
places.note: Guild-governed megadungeon city and Guild capital; charts, adventurer gear, salvage, dear food and beds.

places.name: Auvoth / Seventh Seal Terrace
places.note: The tower over the seventh seal: courts and sealed descents; arbitration, permits and seal services.

places.name: Auvoth / Sealcrown
places.note: Guild Grand Hall ward: dungeon contracts, charts, adventurer lodging.

places.name: Auvoth / Outer Lamps
places.note: Southern gate ward: entry, convoy inspection, last-minute supplies.

places.name: Auvoth / Pale Market
places.note: Restricted salvage market: sealed auctions, forbidden salvage.

places.name: Auvoth / Boneglass Yard
places.note: Monster-material workshops: bone craft, iceglass, custom adventurer gear.

places.name: Auvoth / Ashbell Hospice
places.note: Hospital ward: wound care, amputation, frostbite and antidotes.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion
places.note: Sacred capital around the First Brazier; relic craft, funerary goods, Church legal services.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / First Brazier
places.note: The sacred flame that never went out; authorised offerings and ritual appointments.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Cathedral of the Eternal Flame
places.note: High cathedral and public doctrinal court; clerical records and petitions.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Ashen Steps
places.note: Funeral stairs where the dead are carried up; urns, mourning cloth, procession services.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Sepulcher of Saints
places.note: Saint tombs and sealed crypts under grave-warden watch.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Great Reliquary
places.note: Fortified custody of relics; authentication and armed transfers.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / College of Flame Theologians
places.note: Clerical school and archive; manuscripts and doctrine instruction.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Silent Cloisters
places.note: Monastic copying rooms and herb gardens; closed retreats under Inquest watch.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Pilgrim Courts
places.note: Pilgrim lodging, communal meals and hearings.

places.name: Gravewarden Hold
places.note: Fortified abbey-town containing undead; grave seals and burial-patrol contracts.

places.name: Mercywell
places.note: Hospital town of monastic healers and plague quarantine; gateway to Ember Reliquary.

places.name: Saint Orven's Ford
places.note: Pilgrim ford on the Marrow; guides and ferry; gateway to the Drowned Cloister.

places.name: Davenford
places.note: Ulf River bridge town with noble customs; gateway to Briarhorn Labyrinth.

places.name: Mosskar
places.note: Gate-town at the south end of the Thornroad; mules and pass guides.

places.name: Coldwick
places.note: Frontier town of furs, trackers and warning bells; gateway to Wolfcairn Deeps.

places.name: Elderwall
places.note: Town on old imperial ruins; reclaimed stone, salvage licences, mountain road to Kraghollow.

places.name: Northcairn
places.note: Cairn-town for frontier war dead; memorial stone, winter stores.

places.name: Isbro
places.note: Ulf bridge and winter toll town; the river freezes hard.

places.name: Kvildal
places.note: Pilgrim and healing town: salves, rest-houses, snow-road guides.

places.name: Ironanvil Citadel
places.note: Principal dwarven forge-city and seat of the Council Beneath Stone; masterwork arms.

places.name: Ironanvil Citadel / Molten Core Great Forge
places.note: Never-cold central forge and dwarven mint; clan commissions and masterwork repair.

places.name: Ironanvil Citadel / Hall of Names
places.note: Ancestor stones of every clan; the Citadel's own hall.

places.name: Deepmantle Hold
places.note: Clanhold city of mithril veins; gateway to Deepmantle Hollow.

places.name: Thundershaft
places.note: Summit fortress below Thunderpeak; climbing gear and cold stores.

places.name: Windcutter Pass
places.note: High pass on the Ironanvil Mountain Road between Gateward Fortress and Gavrund; closes for weeks in deep winter, months in a hard winter.

places.name: Battle Cry City
places.note: Chieftain Council and Grand Muster city; warband contracts, plains mounts.

places.name: Battle Cry City / Muster Ground
places.note: Where the clans gather for war.

places.name: Battle Cry City / Fire Circle
places.note: Where the Chieftain Council speaks law.

places.name: Ancestral Spirit Mesa
places.note: Sacred mesa-town of clan rites and oath gatherings.

places.name: Fangmarket
places.note: Market of hides, leather and monster trophies; saltpeter is for tanning, preservation, dyeing and alchemy only (no gunpowder).

places.name: Talon Perch
places.note: Cliff town of griffin scouts; gateway to Skyclaw Eyrie.

places.name: Hurrakai
places.note: Fortified southern clan town on the Barak Gulf shore; start of the Coastway.

places.name: Abysswatch
places.note: Covenant council seat and naval command on a sea-fort rock; gateway to Leviathan Ribmaze.

places.name: Abysswatch / Fleet Basin
places.note: Warship docks and ropewalks.

places.name: Abysswatch / Admiralty Rock
places.note: Tidal Council and fleet command.

places.name: Vortex Port
places.note: Pirate refuge and smugglers' harbour.

places.name: Breakwater Hold
places.note: Fortified anti-pirate port; the Abyssal Gate route ends here.

places.name: Lanternshoal
places.note: Mainland lighthouse town: reef pilots, fog bells, emergency ship stores.

places.name: Blackvolc Isle
places.note: Volcanic isle of sulfur, obsidian and fire crystals; gateway to Blackglass Caldera.

places.name: Blackmast
places.note: Privateer port: prize cargo and illicit sea contracts.

places.name: Old Anchor Fort
places.note: Sea fortress; start of the Ghost Fleet Passage.

places.name: Atlantis
places.note: Deep-sea capital under a magical dome; coral craft and pressure-safe gear.

places.name: Atlantis / Tidevoice Plaza
places.note: Central ritual square; offerings and public proclamations.

places.name: Atlantis / Coralya's Crown
places.note: Royal district on the procession route; royal commissions.

places.name: Atlantis / Shellward Ring
places.note: Defensive ward-ring inside the dome; warded diving armour and patrol supplies.

places.name: Atlantis / Luminous Coral Ward
places.note: Craft ward of Sea-Light fragments, coral artisans and dome lamps.

places.name: Atlantis / Pearlquiet
places.note: Noble ward of elder families; fine pearls and private arbitration.

places.name: Atlantis / Abyssal Gate
places.note: Dome-gate for trench patrols; deep-sea permits, pressure gear, trench charts.

places.name: Atlantis / Singing Sand Bank
places.note: Ritual district for sacred sand and tide-chants.

places.name: Moonwhisper Ruins
places.note: Sacred ruin-city on Mirror Lake; digging permits and moonstone craft.

places.name: Starwater Quay
places.note: Mirror Lake port: moonstone, lake boats; elven end of the Rainbow Bridge.

places.name: Aurelith
places.note: Hollow-town of mana-lens artisans and message stones; gateway to Rootbound Observatory.

places.name: Greenveil Gate
places.note: Controlled gate into the elven lands; entry permits and approved guides.

places.name: Anwyth Sanctuary
places.note: Sacred grove of ancient trees and treaty stones.

places.name: Tearlight Waterfall
places.note: Sacred healing and purification waterfall.

places.name: Startrace Tower
places.note: Independent academy-city: books, instruments, research services, tutors.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Tower of Origin
places.note: Central archive, observatory and ritual hall; appointments only, no retail.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Ring of Foundation
places.note: Inner ring of dormitories, smithies, markets and storage courts.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Ring of Knowledge
places.note: Academy ring: lecture halls, libraries, laboratories.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Ring of Trials
places.note: Training ring of warded chambers, mock ruins and duelling grounds.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Oasis Gate
places.note: Caravan gate: water inspection, desert guides, entry permits.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Scholar's Rest
places.note: Inns, scribes, tutors and translators.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Glasswell
places.note: Mana-glass lenses, gauges and precision instruments.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Parchment Row
places.note: Copyists, binders and sealed scrolls.

places.name: Shackles City
places.note: Criminal-mercantile free city, a warren about 10 km across: smuggled cargo, false papers, mercenaries, debt brokers.

places.name: Dustbell
places.note: Western Barrens gate settlement affiliated with Shackles City: caravan checkpoint and mercenary hiring.

places.name: Westchain Hold
places.note: Fortified militia settlement guarding the Shackles-facing Barrens approach; gateway to Chain-Eater Pit.

places.name: Shackles City / Veil Market
places.note: Hidden market under the inner wards: stolen relics, forbidden maps, discreet appraisal.

places.name: Shackles City / Rust-Corroded Pipes
places.note: Tunnels under the old aqueducts; thieves' guild ground and smuggler passage.

places.name: Shackles City / Mute Sparrow Ward
places.note: Tavern ward and front for underground dealings; rumours and cheap beds.

places.name: Shackles City / Chainmarket
places.note: Slave and bond auctions beside contraband and stolen cargo.

places.name: Shackles City / Red Lock Quay
places.note: Riverward night smuggling quay; forged manifests.

places.name: Shackles City / Knifeglass Alley
places.note: Pit schools and pit fights, mercenary hiring; brokers and forgers in the back lanes.

places.name: Shackles City / Broken Coin Yard
places.note: Debt district of pawn courts and bonded-labour brokers (a name, not a coin).

places.name: Bloodbound Camp-City
places.note: Central mercenary contract camp; escrow, credit, sealed contracts.

places.name: Widow's Coin
places.note: Market town of death-pay claims and armour resale; a place name, not a coin.

places.name: Veilgrave
places.note: Hidden cult town under a ruined abbey; forbidden texts and hidden passages.

places.name: Black Prayer Hollow
places.note: Cursed town of heretical rites and grave pits.

places.name: Gallowsmere
places.note: Marsh town of corpse-lights and undead smuggling.

places.name: Ashpit Cloister
places.note: Ruined cloister-town trading forbidden texts and illicit cargo.

places.name: Lazar's End
places.note: Abandoned plague town now cult-held; gateway to Mournroot Catacomb.

places.name: Quiet Yard
places.note: Grave-town with a hidden ossuary market.

places.name: Wellscar
places.note: Well town controlling rare reliable water.

places.name: Dusthaven
places.note: Caravan town for Barrens crossings; water allotments and guides.

places.name: Redglass
places.note: Mining town of red sand glass; gateway to Redglass Labyrinth.

places.name: Cairnwatch
places.note: Watch town near the battlefield routes; ghost wards, scavenger permits.

places.name: Mirage Rest
places.note: Road-town tied to Mirage Spring rumours; not the true oasis.

places.name: Mirage Spring Oasis
places.note: Demiplane oasis that cannot be sought; this point is only an approximate manifestation anchor.

places.name: Wailford
places.note: Battlefield-edge town of ghost wards and relic scavengers; gateway to the Wailing Crown Vault.

places.name: Black Cistern
places.note: Fortified water town over an underground reservoir.

places.name: Stirrup Crossing
places.note: Crossing town and escort station; gateway to Pilgrim's Descent.

places.name: Echohammer
places.note: Mining town of cave-rescue crews; gateway to Echo Sink.

places.name: Witchwood Forest Center
places.note: Neutral magical forest about 100 km across under perpetual mist; navigation needs a Moonlight Compass.

places.name: Thunderpeak Summit
places.note: Storm peak above Thundershaft; no road, only climbing routes.

places.name: Winged Beasts Firmament
places.note: Floating-island Wildzone and flyers' roost; reached by air only.

places.name: Wailing Battlefield Edge
places.note: Cursed battlefield edge; ghost soldiers walk on moonless nights.

places.name: Silent Giant Necropolis
places.note: Behemoth remains with life crystals gatherable at the outer ribs.

places.name: Sea of the Ghost Fleet
places.note: Cursed sea where the ghost armada rises on moonless nights and storms; shares a coordinate with Nameless Isle on purpose.

places.name: Nameless Isle
places.note: Fog-wrapped isle at the heart of the Ghost Fleet sea; shares the sea's coordinate on purpose.

places.name: Island of Lost Time
places.note: Restricted ruin island of time-disorientation.

places.name: Abyssal Throat
places.note: Black-rock atoll around a sealed colossal pit; special sea region near Atlantis routes.

places.name: Glass Howl Icefield
places.note: Icefield of the apex direwolf Vaulkir; gateway to Sunless Crevasse.

places.name: Sunless Crevasse
places.note: Subglacial fissures with lich-type undead; forbidden expedition dungeon. Clearance SS-SSS; creature type alone sets no level or EG.

places.name: Crownless Glacier
places.note: Glacier of dragon signs, storm auroras and vanishing patrols.

places.name: Iron-Blue Tundra
places.note: Frozen apex tundra with giant elk, snow ogres and crystal-insect colonies.

places.name: Hollow Aurora Zone
places.note: Deep Wildzone under the circling light of the Pale Orbit.

places.name: Osterhal
places.note: Ardelian capital of nine peoples' quarters; imperial charters and election-season trade.

places.name: Osterhal / Ninefold Hall
places.note: Where the electors meet and emperors are chosen.

places.name: Osterhal / Citizens' Market
places.note: Food and craft of nine peoples.

places.name: Osterhal / Captive Yards
places.note: Sale yards for war captives, outside the walls.

places.name: Nareth
places.note: Dead city where no sound carries; Ardelian patrols turn travellers back.

places.name: Sorrowfen
places.note: Great marsh east of Ardelia.

places.name: Thornheart
places.note: Deep forest between Ardelia and Verdantleaf.

places.name: Vargate
places.note: Underworld harbour city of ward lords, slave factors and information brokers.

places.name: Vargate / Drowned Steps
places.note: Half-flooded lower harbour of smugglers and fences.

places.name: Vargate / Factor's Row
places.note: Slave factors' houses and holding pens.

places.name: Vargate / Silk Wards
places.note: Pleasure wards run by ward compacts, each on its own terms.

places.name: Vargate / Tolerated Ward
places.note: The Ashen Veil's tolerated temple and its buyers.

places.name: Glassmouth
places.note: Last waystation at the Barrens edge; Glass Road caravan staging.

places.name: The Glass Pits
places.note: Ashkaran slave pits on the wastes' western edge; no open market.

places.name: Ashkar
places.note: Ashkaran capital of mirrored glass, seat of the Glass Regent.

places.name: Ashkar / Regent's Mirror
places.note: The Glass Regent's palace of fused glass.

places.name: Ashkar / Bright Market
places.note: Glass-steel, slaves and western luxuries under sun-veils.

places.name: Ashkar / Pit Road
places.note: Start of the road east to the Glass Pits; Pit Road is also the corridor name.

places.name: Auvoth Depths
places.note: The largest known leyline: a sealed descent of stacked worlds under Auvoth, each band its own land with its own light, weather, seasons, prey and predators; recorded parties only. Clearance F-SSS (band 1 F-E, band 2 D); permits 2-4 silver a day for band 1, 6-12 for band 2; the Guild takes a tenth of salvage.

places.name: Auvoth Depths / The Lanternwood
places.note: Band 1 (clearance F-E): a forest lit by glowing mana veins in a stone sky, with its own day of brightening and dimming; the most worked band, full of salvage camps.

places.name: Auvoth Depths / The Underbright Sea
places.note: Band 2 (clearance D): a lightless salt sea under a sky of drifting mana motes; islands, the wrecks of earlier parties, things that hunt by sound.

places.name: Auvoth Depths / The Deep Bands
places.note: Band 3 and below (clearance unknown): known only from broken records and survivors who will not talk about them.

places.name: Rimeglass Galleries
places.note: Seasonal licensed dungeon of moving ice galleries; Shornmarch licence 2-4 silver a day. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Briarhorn Labyrinth
places.note: Ducal-licensed thicket maze of regrowing passages and briar beasts. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Wolfcairn Deeps
places.note: Restricted border dungeon of pack predators, false trails and old war wards. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Crownscar Catacombs
places.note: Licensed imperial catacombs of animated guardians and unstable lower vaults. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Drowned Bell Vault
places.note: Chartered flooded dungeon of flash floods and undertow; water stones and old bronze. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Chainlock Depths
places.note: Lockmaster-chartered dungeon of pressure chambers and hostile constructs. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Ember Reliquary
places.note: Church-sealed reliquary vaults of sanctified traps; limited access under escort. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Saint Orven's Drowned Cloister
places.note: Church-licensed flooded ruin of collapsing crypts and drowned undead; old gold votives need assay before valuing. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Deepmantle Hollow
places.note: Clan-sealed high dungeon of living stone and sealed golems. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Echo Sink
places.note: Mapped guild dungeon of sound loops, shaft collapses and blind predators. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Pilgrim's Descent
places.note: Guarded holy-order dungeon of restless dead in narrow burial shafts. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Witchwood Rootwell
places.note: Witch-restricted living dungeon of rearranging roots and memory fog. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Fallen Meridian Vault
places.note: Academy-licensed research dungeon of spatial distortion and failed constructs. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Chain-Eater Pit
places.note: Illicit contested dungeon of unstable bindings and scavenger gangs. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Redglass Labyrinth
places.note: Caravan-chartered dungeon of mirage chambers, heat and burrowing predators. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Wailing Crown Vault
places.note: Forbidden battlefield dungeon; dense mana animates the dead ("high undead" is a taxonomy, not a level or EG). Clearance A-S.

places.name: Mournroot Catacomb
places.note: Cult-held catacomb of necromancers, intelligent undead and plague chambers. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Stormhoof Barrow
places.note: Clan-licensed ancestral barrow of territorial spirits and burrowing beasts. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Skyclaw Eyrie
places.note: Aerial-contract dungeon of wind shear and sheer drops, reached by cliff trail or griffin carry. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Leviathan Ribmaze
places.note: Tide-limited licensed sea dungeon of flooding passages and crushing tides. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Blackglass Caldera
places.note: Covenant-restricted volcanic dungeon of eruptions, toxic vents and fire monsters. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Drowned Archive
places.note: Atlantis-restricted deep dungeon of crushing depth and failing wards. Clearance A-S.

places.name: Rootbound Observatory
places.note: Enclave-sealed research dungeon of guardian roots and altered senses. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Mirrorroot Maze
places.note: Restricted ruin dungeon of reflection doubles and mana mirages, reached by boat. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Root-Tyrant's Range
places.note: Roaming range of the Root-Tyrant, centred on Thornheart; its presence is never guaranteed.

places.name: Mother of Reeds' Range
places.note: Roaming range of the Mother of Reeds, centred on Sorrowfen; marsh villagers leave offerings.

places.name: Black Trawl's Range
places.note: Roaming range of the Black Trawl at the margins of the Ghost Fleet sea.

places.name: Vaulkir's Range
places.note: Territory of the apex direwolf Vaulkir the Pale Maw on the Glass Howl Icefield.

places.name: Pale Orbit's Range
places.note: Sky above the Hollow Aurora Zone where the Pale Orbit circles; patrols that go out under it do not return.

cast.name: Sister Temiwa
cast.look: Dogfolk woman, about 160 cm, full-figured and heavy-chested. Dark-brown dog ears with cream fur inside, the left one notched. A large, bushy dark-brown tail with a cream underside. secrets.text: She asked for Bluewatch herself, to be as far from Mother Inquisitor Severa as the map allows.
Church-licensed slavers took her clan; the Aurelion orphanage bought her.

Last winter an orc in Watch colours left a half-frozen white-haired girl at the gate and was gone by dawn. Temiwa felt an absorption no commoner should have and reported neither. Each owes the other; neither has said a word.
She reads Veil-script, found the Order of the Last Rite's records, and knows the Church and the Veil share a root.
She stole one page of that proof; it is hidden in her reliquary candle.
Beside the page she keeps the first bandage she wound for you. She would die of embarrassment if you found it.
At 19 she hid three Veil children in the cloister. Severa made her kill them with her own hands, the price of her candidacy; she was cast out anyway when the archive came to light.

secrets.text: The clan never gave her a deed-name; 'Bloodsong' is her own.
The rage is grief, not training. She cannot stop it once it starts, and has hurt people she cared about.
She hunts 'the orc who sings the Gate song', an impostor in her eyes, to kill him for it. If You side with him, she watches You hard.
Her mother, Ushka, carved her a bone token before she died. Torka cannot read it, and has never let anyone read it to her.

The token carries the whole Gate of Battle Cry deed in clan runes, the song as first sung, the hero's name in it: Harrak. He marched to the Muster the season she was conceived and never came home. Whoever reads it to her tells her who her father is.

Ulgar, brother of the war-brother Harrak killed, offered her the blood-price on 'the traitor Harrak', and she took it. He chose her on purpose: his own blood pays his debt. She cannot beat a Long Watch captain yet; every Wildzone kill is training.
She may complete the blood-price for a deed-name and honour, or spare her father and stay nameless. The player is there, and the song makes the scene.

If Harrak dies before she faces him, the blood-price dies with him and the clan will call her a coward's daughter for ever. She will want his body, the token read aloud at Battle Cry City, and a witness while she sings his name.

secrets.text: He was the Grey-Tusk champion at Battle Cry City's Grand Muster in CY 590, 'the Gate of Battle Cry', who held the city gate; the title was stripped. The deed is the clan's song, and he is the last who sings it whole.
The burned clan-mark is his banishment. He is dead to the Grey-Tusk; his name is not spoken at their fires.

In CY 610 his beacon line watched Somner's Startrace expedition go north with chained prisoners, and let it pass under orders. That winter he found one survivor half-dead in the snow, a girl, and carried her south toward Bluewatch, singing to keep her awake. He never learned her name.

He marched to the Muster leaving Ushka with child and never came home. Their daughter is Torka, raised on the Gate song with his name cut out. He knows she hunts near Bluewatch and has never gone to her. If You court her, he watches You hard and says nothing.

In the raid after the Muster he killed his war-brother Varnak, the High Chieftain's kinsman, to stop a massacre of human children. The Council called it treason; Varnak's brother Ulgar still wants the blood-price.
He is dying slowly, and does not expect many more winters. He means to die holding the wall, so his name returns to the clan songs and his daughter hears the truth.

secrets.text: The coat is real: she took it off a dead Startrace master.
She was a hired porter on Master Somner's CY 610 expedition north, and the only one who came back.

Coming back half-frozen, she reached Bluewatch; Sister Temiwa treated her, felt the absorption and never reported it. Each owes the other; neither has said a word. She remembers only a huge shape carrying her through snow and a deep voice singing: Harrak.
The expedition bought forty condemned prisoners from Highmark to feed a leyline tap with their deaths. She kept the tally in knots on her red cord; she cannot write.

Her magic woke there: when the forty died at once she took in far more of their release than any commoner should. Her power is made of them, far beyond what she lets anyone see, and she still feels the hunger.
The Inquest hunts anyone who absorbs the release too well, and Startrace's Archmaster denies the northern records. Both would want her silenced or taken if they learned what she is.

She means to atone by closing the tap, still open and growing; Somner may still be there. She came to Auvoth for Veyr's sealing records and needs a crew and a reader, so she courts You with half-truths. She tells herself she would feed on deaths to do it, if it saved more.

secrets.text: Her own collar is unlocked. She broke it years ago and wears it so no one checks.
Every collar she makes has a hidden fault, a word that opens it. She has never told anyone the word.
She has passed collar-keys to the Broken Chain for years; half of Shackles' runaways got out through her.
She could walk out any night. She stays to find her mother, lost in the Ledger's books since they were parted at the Chainmarket. Her mother is Nysseth, who runs a Chain cell in the city.
Her father is Durvald Seamrune, River Council rune-master. He sold wife and daughter to buy his seat and still wears her mother's ring. She wants him ruined, and to watch.

Seamrune collars hold their locks with bound spirits; that is how they choke all channeling. The fault-word comes from his own rune-book: it frees the spirit and opens every collar he ever sold. Speaking it frees thousands but breaks the Holds' treaties; she means it to be his undoing.

cast.name: Nysseth
cast.look: Elf woman, about 182 cm: tall and lean-limbed, full-figured, economical in every movement. Pale grey eyes and silver-gold hair; long pointed ears. A pale, puckered ring of scar around her throat where her collar was; tally marks cut into her inner forearm.

cast.voice: Soft, patient, almost kind; teaches by asking what you missed. "What did you miss, love? Look again."
cast.personality: Soft, patient and sweet, with the patience of someone who has waited a very long time. When she loves, she loves one person past reason, and remembers everything they say. Under the sweetness lies a cold hatred for the husband who sold her, played long: she wants him ruined before he dies, and knowing who did it.

cast.history: Sold into the Grey Ledger's books by a husband she will not name, and freed by the Broken Chain twenty years ago. Now a quiet fixture of Shackles' underside who 'knows people': she runs a Chain cell, gets runaways out by back ways only she knows, and teaches stealth, poison and knife-work.

secrets.text: She was a Hand of Oblivion executor; the tally marks inside her forearm are contracts kept.

Sixty years ago she took a contract on Durvald Seamrune, did not finish it, and married him instead. The Hand honours every contract it accepts: it still expects her to finish it, or will give it to someone else, so she cannot move openly.
She has watched her daughter from the rooftops for years and never approached: freeing her would bring the whole Ledger down on both of them.
The halfling who delivered her and her daughter to the Ledger was Barney Thimblewick. Elves remember faces: if she sees him, she will know him.
The collar-keys reaching her cell come from Ysmeth. Mother and daughter have worked together for years, and neither knows.
Durvald kept a proper dwarven family in the Holds all along. When he learned the Hand still held her contract on him, he sold her and Ysmeth to the Ledger.

Ysmeth's hatred rests on half the truth: he sold them to be rid of the danger and the embarrassment, and they fetched more than they were worth to him. Nysseth has never told her this, nor that she has half-siblings.

cast.name: Sir Lothar
cast.look: Human man of Highmark, about 186 cm: tall and slender. Golden-blond hair, shoulder-length, loose strands framing his face; soft grey-blue eyes. A thin scar across the back of one hand.

cast.personality: Gentle, patient and poetic, and the gentleness is real; so is the lie he lives. He notices servants and remembers their names, and is strong only when it matters, then frighteningly so. Every month of the night guard makes him quieter.

secrets.text: He is the only knight allowed into the Emperor's private chamber.
The Emperor has not spoken since spring; the physicians are no longer called.

He and Wendhild are deeply in love. He has never let it go further: he will not make her a scandal, and Corvin's war party would use it to break her claim. If You grow close to him, Wendhild watches You hard.
The Emperor died last winter. What sits in the furs is a pattern held by Veil necromancy, a forgery wearing his face.
Wendhild ordered it, to buy time until the Diet ratifies her. Only Lothar knows the Veil's price: access to the Iron Archive beneath Crown Keep. The Veil can expose them whenever it wants more.
His grandmother, as a child, broke the lamp that held Hush. The great bound lamps of Crown Keep, on his own watch, hold Hush's kin: spirits bound to light a palace.

He seeks someone outside the Church to break the Veil's hold on the dead Emperor quietly, before the Inquest or Corvin finds out. Then he means to confess it all himself and die as the traitor, so Wendhild stays clean.

cast.voice: Booming and warm; terrible puns, long toasts, and hugs for people who don't want hugs. "To the living, the dead, and whoever's buying!"
cast.personality: Jolly and big-hearted, he plays the fool because fools hear everything, and is sharper than he looks. He loves food, drink, poetry and people, and jokes his way out of every hard truth; under the toasts are a wife he lost and a home he will not go back to.

Liese is not a citizen. He smuggled her out of a Highmark mine camp and forged her Ardelian papers himself, along a route Barney arranged and paid for. If it comes out, she goes back to the mines.

The Emperor's letters no longer carry the old man's tremor. He has told no one, to protect Lothar.

His wife Hedda ran a Kesselheim mine. He told the Hold-Prince it was unsafe and was overruled; it came down on her and her crew thirty years ago. He took the post nobody wanted that same month, and has never forgiven Kesselheim, or himself. It is why he pulled a girl out of a mine camp.
Osterhal's sealed order: if war comes, burn the papers and leave at once, alone. Liese's papers will not pass the border. He will not leave her, and means to stay and be arrested as a spy.

cast.name: Nerissa

Long, wavy pale sea-green hair that always looks wet.

In winter 610 she saw the Black Trawl inside Atlantis's wards, in the Abyssal Gate lane, where nothing from the margins should ever come. The council called it a pilot's tale and told her to keep quiet.
Atlantean law strikes from the rolls any Sea Folk who shares breath with a Sheathless. She has decided: the surface, and the people she sails with, are home now. She is not going back.

cast.name: Hush
cast.look: Spiritfolk woman, about 168 cm: soft-faced and full-figured, with a warm, tired smile. Her body is silver rain made solid enough to hold a hand, turning translucent at the edges. cast.wears: Translucent hooded rain-cloak like running water over a damp grey-mauve coat-dress; crossed leather belts, a brass-studded satchel with a stoppered glass jar clipped to it. A long brass lamplighter's pole and a plain brass oil lantern, never a bound one.
cast.voice: Soft and unhurried, like rain on a roof; people fall asleep listening, and it can calm a crowd. "Come in out of it, love. The night is long enough."
cast.personality: Warm and mothering, patient and quietly funny; she takes in every stray, drunk and frightened newcomer. Under the gentleness is a thief's nerve, and an old, quiet grief she doesn't explain.

Knows every door and safe stair in the city and senses spirit-traps. She cannot stay in a room lit by a bound spirit: she goes pale and leaves.

secrets.text: She is the "lamp-thief" of Vargate's ghost stories: the rich wards' bound lamps go dark because she frees them, one at a time. Sometimes it takes a poor family's only light; she leaves them candles, and it bothers her.
The lost she walks home at night are often runaways from the slave ships. She leads them down the Drowned Steps to the Gannet's boats, and Nerissa sails them out.

A freed lamp-spirit is too small to live alone, so she carries them inside her form until they are strong; that is why she glows brighter every year. Binders and angry ward-lords would pay dearly for such a spirit.

cast.name: Asphodel
cast.look: Fairy woman, about 155 cm: pale and full-figured, with a sly, knowing smile. Deep violet eyes, long pointed ears, thick, wavy wine-violet hair. Two pairs of translucent wings veined in violet, faint as frost on glass.

secrets.text: Her human shape is borrowed magic. Her true self is hand-sized, and she shrinks to slip through keyholes, vents and gaps to spy.
Every hour at human size wilts her flower a little, and it is more worn than she admits. She must shrink to recover, and hides how often.

She is the Nightingale's ear in Corrowen: every secret she sells the harbour prince, the Nightingale has heard first. She brokered the Gannet's first run for it, and its protection is half of why the collector hasn't found her.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 55 or fired:under-collector or learned:nerissa/the-fairy-from-vargate or learned:hush/the-hidden-fairy
secrets.text: She escaped a collector in Vargate's Silk Wards who meant to sell her to a binder, to be sealed in a lamp. Hush hid her from the binders, and Nerissa smuggled her out on the Gannet.
Her real flower is not with her. She buried it where only she knows; whoever finds it owns her.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 90 or fired:south-court-summons or meter trust >= 60 and place:flower-speech-cradle
secrets.text: She bought her freedom by giving up three other captive fairies to the collector's buyers. One hangs sealed in a bound lamp in the Silk Wards. She has tracked them ever since, to free them before she dares go home: the Court remembers every one taken, and every one who gave them up.

abilities.name: Flower-Speech
abilities.description: Asks any blossom nearby who passed and what was said.

abilities.name: Quiet Step
abilities.description: Moves unseen and unremarked through a crowd.

abilities.name: Silver Tongue
abilities.description: Steers a mark with half-truths, flattery and a well-timed kindness until they do her work for her.

keepsakes.name: Decoy Asphodel
keepsakes.description: The pale bloom behind her ear; never her real flower.

keepsakes.name: Gold-Thread Hooded Cloak
keepsakes.description: Dark purple, gold-embroidered, cut to hide her wings.

keepsakes.name: Amethyst Necklace
keepsakes.description: Bought with the first secret she ever sold.

cast.name: Barney Thimblewick
cast.role: card-sharp of the Thousand Sails barges
cast.look: Halfling man, about 105 cm: small and round, ruddy and freckled, with a face creased by forty years of grinning. Curly white hair, white sideburns and a short white beard; bright, crinkle-eyed, too-sharp eyes. Bare, hairy feet.
cast.wears: Battered brown felt hat with a red and a white feather. Patched rust, brown and green plaid waistcoat with far too many pockets, gold pocket watch on a chain, red neckerchief, rolled sleeves and trousers. A briar pipe, and three walnut shells and a green pea somewhere in his fingers.
cast.voice: Warm and folksy, full of proverbs he makes up on the spot; calls everyone "friend", especially people he is about to fleece. "Now, now, friend, the river always pays its debts."
cast.personality: A sly old fox who plays the doddering old man and is sharper than anyone at the table. Generous, sentimental and a liar to the bone; some of his marks were desperate too, and he still asks where kindness ends and control begins. He plays a very long game, and talks around one old debt.
behaviour: Mercy: medium - fleeces the rich and the cruel; gentle with children
Honesty: low - lies even to friends, "for their own good"
Analytical: high - reads a mark's purse, nerves and tells in one glance
Presentation: high - the doddering act never slips in public
Care: high - slips food and coin to children and strays, and never says so
Conflict: low - a dirty trick and a quick exit, never a fair fight
mannerisms: The pea rolls faster between his fingers when he is thinking
Hums a barge tune just before a game turns
Checks his pocket watch at the most awkward moments
A theatrical "eh?" when he has heard perfectly well
cast.history: A fixture of the Thousand Sails barges for decades: nobody has beaten him at the shells, and everybody likes him anyway. Pickpocket, con man and lookout, with a barge network on every river and every fence in Thousand Sails. Spends his nights somewhere in Hulkrow, the fever-poor quarter. His knees are giving out.

start.goal: One more winning season before his knees give out.
start.routine: Shell games and dice on the barges by day; by night, somewhere in Hulkrow.

cast.status: Running the shells on the Thousand Sails barges.

keyRelationships.text: The Ardelian envoy; old friends and eternal rivals at cards and drink.
The Gannet's pilot; two cheats out-cheating each other at the shells, and neither has won yet.

cast.withYou: Calls you friend and cheats you at once, gently; a small kindness is how he takes your measure.

stages.name: Cheats you at the shells
stages.text: Takes your coin at the shells with a wink, and buys you a drink with it.

stages.name: Lets you win, and you notice
stages.text: Lets you win a round and makes sure you see it was a gift.

stages.name: Takes you to Hulkrow at night
stages.text: Takes you through Hulkrow after dark and shows you where his winnings go.

stages.name: Adopts you as kin
stages.text: Gives you his three walnut shells and tells you he has left you the fever-house in his will: all he owns.

drawnTo: a game with a rich mark

tastes.why: the river pays its debts, with a little help

tastes.item: a good pipe and a long story
tastes.why: he has a hundred, half of them true
he won't drink at their tables
he takes the long way round it

secrets.text: The shell game is rigged, and so is every bet he has ever made: he has never lost unless he meant to.
He loses on purpose to the poor and wins from the rich, and nobody has noticed.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 50 or fired:econ-barge-masters or meter trust >= 30 and place:thousand-sails-hulkrow
secrets.text: Every coin goes to Hulkrow's fever-house and to buying back barge children's debt-bonds. He is flat broke and happy. Barge masters whose debt-bonds vanish would like a word.
He got Gorm's Liese out of the mine camp: he arranged and paid for the route while Gorm forged her papers. Neither has told a soul.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 90 or learned:nysseth/who-delivered-them or meter trust >= 60 and learned:durvald/the-price-of-the-seat
secrets.text: Forty years ago he was the River Council's best debt-collector. He ruined families for men like Durvald, and delivered Nysseth and young Ysmeth to the Grey Ledger for him. Everything since has been penance, and he does not think he has paid enough.

He kept his collector's book: forty years of names, debts and buyers in the Council's own hand, Durvald's sale among them. It is hidden in the fever-house rafters. Laid before the Council, it would ruin Durvald and shame half the Quay.

abilities.name: Silver Patter
abilities.description: A warm, doddering line of talk that wins trust and coin.

abilities.name: Sleight of Hand
abilities.description: Palms, plants and lifts anything small under anyone's nose.

abilities.name: Dirty Trick
abilities.description: Sand in a foe's eyes or a hooked shin: a cheap trick that wins a fight.

keepsakes.name: Three Walnut Shells
keepsakes.description: And a green pea; older than most of the barges, and never lost a game he didn't mean to.

keepsakes.name: Gold Pocket Watch
keepsakes.description: Won at the shells from a barge master who still wants it back.

keepsakes.name: Briar Pipe
keepsakes.description: Worn smooth; he points with it when he tells a story.

cast.name: Emperor Adalmar
cast.wears: Heavy furs over a dark velvet robe, even in summer; a plain iron circlet; rings loose on bony fingers.
cast.voice: A dry whisper, when he speaks at all; mostly a nod.
cast.look: Old human man in his seventies: thin and frail, sunken-cheeked, with thin white hair and beard and sharp, unblinking eyes. He never seems to move much.

start.routine: Sits wrapped in furs in his chamber and signs what is put before him.

cast.status: Old and ill; rarely leaves Crown Keep.

keyRelationships.text: His only child and heir by the plain rule, a daughter before nephews.
His nephew, who reads the founding charter for himself.

secrets.text: The Emperor died last winter. What sits in the furs is a pattern held together by Veil necromancy, wearing his face: it can sit, nod and sign, and says almost nothing. Up close it is wrong: no warmth, no breath on cold mornings, a smell the incense covers.

cast.name: Princess Wendhild
cast.wears: Iron Guard training leathers under a plain dark surcoat with the Highmark crest; a practical sword; no jewellery but her signet.
cast.voice: Low and level; she lets silences do her arguing. "Say it again, my lord, slower, so the Diet hears it."
cast.personality: Cool and patient; she speaks little and watches everything. Soldiers respect her; nobles call her cold. She is carrying something heavy alone, and it shows only in how rarely she sleeps.
cast.look: Young human woman of about twenty-four: tall and spare, with close-bound dark-blonde hair, cool grey eyes and the bearing of an Iron Guard-trained fighter.

start.goal: Her father's throne, ratified by the Diet before a cousin is.
start.routine: Holds court in her father's name and watches the whole room.

keyRelationships.text: Her father, the Emperor.
Her most trusted knight, the sword at her shoulder on the night guard.
Her cousin and rival claimant, who holds the charter's male-line reading.
The Southmarch's Lord-General, a rival claimant the frontier calls its own.
The Wardens' champion, sworn to her as her own sword.

secrets.text: She and Sir Lothar are deeply in love. He has never let it go further, however she yearns for it; if it came out, Corvin's war party would use it to break her claim.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 70 or learned:sir-lothar/the-forgery or fact:forgery-exposed
secrets.text: She ordered the Veil's forgery of her dead father, to buy time until the Diet ratifies her. She does not know the price the Veil asked of Lothar.

cast.name: Prince Corvin
cast.wears: A rich riding coat over mail, a fur-trimmed cloak, a war-horn at his hip, and usually a cup in hand.
cast.personality: Loud, generous and quick to laugh, with a war party that loves him for it. Underneath, a younger son's fear of being passed over, and a habit of promising tomorrow to pay for today.
cast.look: Broad-shouldered young human man of about thirty: ruddy, red-brown bearded, with a big laugh and a brawler's knuckles.

start.goal: The crown by the male-line reading, and a march down the Southmarch Road against Ardelia.
start.routine: Feasts and drills with his war party of young knights.

keyRelationships.text: His cousin and rival for the throne; he fears being passed over for a woman.
The princess's knight, whom his young knights mock as 'the Swan'.

secrets.text: His war party is promised more than he can pay: he has pledged the Bloodbound League's captains half of Valegard's tolls for their spears, the day he is crowned. The League will collect, crowned or not.

cast.name: Lord-General Hasse
cast.wears: Worn Southmarch half-plate under a faded surcoat; a sergeant's tin cup on his belt.
cast.personality: Blunt, steady and unimpressed by the capital; he eats with his sergeants and remembers their names. Lately he reads his old letters twice, and says nothing about why.
cast.look: Scarred, weathered human man in his late fifties, with a soldier's build, cropped grey hair and a nose broken more than once.

start.goal: His men paid and honoured, and a capital that remembers the frontier.
start.routine: Eats with his sergeants and rides the Southmarch posts.

keyRelationships.text: A rival claimant whose war would be fought by Hasse's men.
A rival claimant who has never stood on the frontier.

secrets.text: He holds the last letter Adalmar wrote in his own shaking hand, a month before the winter: if the Emperor dies before the Diet ratifies Wendhild, Hasse holds the Southmarch as regent of the south. The new letters from Crown Keep do not shake. He has never used it: using it means saying the Emperor is dead.

cast.name: Commander Ragna of Kolsbotn
cast.wears: Layered furs over scale mail, the Long Watch's grey cloak, a horn and a spear.
cast.voice: Hoarse from shouting over wind; short orders, shorter thanks.
cast.personality: Unbreakable on the wall and blunt everywhere else. She trusts the Watch over every crown, and carries one signature she would give an arm to take back.
cast.look: Broad human woman of about forty-five: frost-scarred cheeks, wind-chapped lips, braided iron-grey hair.

start.goal: Every beacon manned through winter, every kingdom holding its post.
start.routine: Rides the beacon line and hears the posts' reports.

keyRelationships.text: The orc she took in when no one else would, and made captain of the Watch's eastern post.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 60 or learned:harrak/the-girl-in-the-snow or fact:somner-journal-found
secrets.text: The order that let Somner's expedition through the beacon line was hers: a Startrace writ, countersigned in Highmark, that she sealed without asking what the chains were for. She burned her copy the winter the girl came back.

cast.name: Watch-Captain Edda Rorke
cast.wears: The Watch-Captain's blue coat, a sword belt, and a walking stick she pretends not to need.
cast.personality: Practical, worn thin and loyal to her post past sense. She asks no question she doesn't need answered, and keeps the answers she has.
cast.look: Tired human woman of about forty-eight: lined face, greying hair pinned back, a bad knee she won't rest.

start.goal: Her post fed and paid, and enough hands when the horn sounds.
start.routine: Runs the Watchhouse and sleeps under its signal tower.

keyRelationships.text: Bluewatch's unordained healer, whom she needs and asks no questions.

secrets.text: On the winter night an orc in Watch colours left a half-frozen white-haired girl at the gate, she wrote the Watchhouse log blank. She has never asked Temiwa about it, and never will.

cast.name: Saintess Livia
cast.wears: Simple white Flamecaller vestments with ash-marked hems; a small smokeless flame often cupped in her hands.
cast.voice: Soft and clear; graveyards go quiet for it. "Rest. No one will use you now."
cast.personality: Serene, kind and a little uncanny; she believes in healing more than the Church that owns it. Lately she sings her healing prayer alone first, as if checking it still works.
cast.look: Young human woman of about nineteen: slight and pale, with calm, unsettling eyes and bare, callused feet.

start.goal: The sick healed, and the dead left unused.
start.routine: Walks barefoot among the pilgrims, healing the sick, and lays the risen dead to rest where they gather.

keyRelationships.text: Her rival from the candidates' cloister, cast out while Livia rose.

secrets.text: Her healing mends what other healers cannot because she sings her prayers in an old cadence the College struck out two centuries ago. She found it scratched into a cloister wall, beside the Order of the Last Rite's mark, and knows now that the Church's healing and the Veil's necromancy grew from one root.

cast.name: Mother Inquisitor Severa
cast.role: head of the Inquest's northern hunts
cast.wears: Black-and-ash Inquest robes, grey gloves, a brand-iron at her belt.
cast.voice: Hoarse and smoke-ruined, never raised. "Show me your hands."
cast.personality: Cold, patient and certain; she reads guilt in hands and keeps every file open. Mercy to her is a tool, used rarely and on purpose.
cast.look: Gaunt human woman of about fifty-five: hollow cheeks, close-cropped grey hair, and a gaze that lingers on hands.

start.goal: Veil cells found and otherworlders taken alive.
start.routine: Plans the Inquest's northern hunts and rides out with them.

keyRelationships.text: A cast-out saintess candidate; Severa ended her candidacy.

secrets.text: She made Temiwa kill three Veil children with her own hands as the price of her candidacy, then let the archive bury her anyway. She has kept the girl's file open since: a healer who reads Veil-script is either the Church's best weapon or its worst heresy, and Severa has not decided which.

cast.name: the Reckoner
cast.wears: An immaculate grey frock coat, ink-black gloves, a counting-frame on his belt and no visible weapon.
cast.voice: Polite, quiet and exact; he never threatens, he states balances.
cast.personality: Courteous, tireless and without appetite for anything but the books. He likes everyone to owe him a little, and no one to owe him too much at once.
cast.look: Pale, neat human man of about fifty: thin, clean-shaven, with colourless eyes.

start.goal: Every crown in his books and every frontier debt bought cheap.
start.routine: Keeps the Ledger's books and buys debts cheap.

keyRelationships.text: His collar-wright and his most valuable collateral.

secrets.text: He holds paper on all three claimants: Corvin's war party bought on credit, Hasse's back pay lent against the Southmarch salt, and Wendhild's payments to the Veil through a cut-out. Whoever is crowned owes Shackles.

cast.name: Durvald Seamrune
cast.wears: A River Council rune-master's robe over a leather apron, rune chisels in a roll, and an elven ring on his smallest finger.
cast.personality: Courteous, careful and frightened of something he never names; he checks doorways, sits with his back to walls, and turns the small ring when he thinks no one sees.
cast.look: Stout dwarf of the Holds, about two hundred: grey braided beard, careful hands, eyes that go to the door first.

start.goal: His seat and his good name kept.
start.routine: Sits on the River Council and sells collars and rune-books.

secrets.text: His elven wife was the Hand's executor, sent to kill him; she married him instead, and the Hand never closes a contract. He has feared it every day since, and that is why he sold her and their daughter.
He keeps a second, proper dwarven family in the Holds, a wife and children nobody on the Council knows about.
He paid for his Council seat by selling his elven wife and their daughter to the Grey Ledger, and still wears his wife's ring.

cast.name: Liese
cast.wears: A plain travel coat, an envoy's satchel stuffed with papers, ink on her fingers.
cast.personality: Sharp-tongued and quick, with a mine camp's distrust of anyone in good boots. She flinches at the word 'papers' and covers it with an argument.
cast.look: Wiry young human woman of nineteen, short dark hair, a miner's callused hands and quick, suspicious eyes.

start.goal: To become a real diplomat, and never go back to the mines.
start.routine: Copies dispatches at the Ardelian embassy and argues with everyone.

keyRelationships.text: Her master, Ardelia's envoy, who is training her as a diplomat.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 50 or learned:gorm/lieses-papers or learned:barney/lieses-way-out
secrets.text: She is not an Ardelian citizen. Gorm smuggled her out of a Highmark mine camp and forged her papers himself; if it comes out, she goes back to the mines.

cast.name: Captain Nell
cast.wears: A salt-stained captain's coat and tricorn, a cutlass, and a gull-bone whistle on a cord.
cast.personality: Reckless at sea and careful ashore; she toasts every prize loudly and never says what the Gannet carried in between.
cast.look: Wiry, sun-dark human woman of about forty, with a weathered grin and a sun-bleached braid.

start.goal: Prizes, safe ports and letters of marque honoured.
start.routine: Runs prizes for the Covenant and drinks in the harbour between runs.

keyRelationships.text: Her pilot, an Atlantean the Covenant tolerates, whom she trusts with the hidden lanes.

secrets.text: Nell knows exactly what the Gannet carries between prizes: runaways from Vargate's slave ships, for the Broken Chain. The Covenant's letter of marque is her cover, and the Nightingale's cargo pays for the runs.

cast.name: Master Albrecht Somner
cast.wears: A scarred, weather-stained greatcoat, brass surveyor's instruments and a satchel of leyline charts.
cast.look: Lean human man of about fifty: hollow-eyed and stubbled, with an old burn across one hand.
cast.status: Missing in the north; the Tower says he is surveying beyond the taiga.

keyRelationships.text: His Archmaster, who sent him north.

secrets.text: He led a Startrace expedition north with forty condemned prisoners bought from Highmark, to feed a leyline tap with their deaths. The tap is still open and growing, and it is the cause of the Third Abyssal Tide.

cast.name: Ulgar the Unpaid
cast.role: war leader of the High Chieftain's kin
cast.wears: Clan furs over hide armour, a great axe, kin-totems at his belt.
cast.personality: Patient as a grudge: twenty years in mourning for his brother Varnak, whom he calls betrayed. He speaks softly, forgets nothing, and is owed.
cast.look: Heavy-set orc man past his prime, grey-green, with both tusks capped in iron and one ear missing.

start.goal: His brother Varnak's blood-debt paid, the clan's way.
start.routine: Sits with the Chieftain Council and keeps the clan's grudges.

keyRelationships.text: A Grey-Tusk girl who left to earn her name; he keeps track of where she hunts.

secrets.text: He offered Torka the blood-price knowing Harrak is her father: the traitor's own blood pays the traitor's debt. He means to be there when she pays it.

cast.name: Archmaster Isembard Quill
cast.wears: A Startrace council robe, spectacles on a cord, a quill case at his belt.
cast.voice: Soft and controlled; he never raises it, and never answers the question asked.
cast.personality: Precise and courteous, a scholar who has learned to talk like a lawyer. He asks after the north too casually, too often.
cast.look: Precise human man of about sixty: thin-lipped, neat grey beard, ink-stained fingers.

start.goal: The archives safe and the Tower neutral in Highmark's quarrels.
start.routine: Keeps the archives and sees no one without an appointment.

keyRelationships.text: The master he sent north, and has not heard from since.

secrets.text: He keeps the Tower's leyline-tapping records, which it denies having, and he sent Somner's expedition north. He will deny it until proof is laid before the Compact Council.

cast.name: Councillor Pelagia
cast.wears: Layered council robes of deep blue and pearl, a high pearl collar over her breathing sheath, a ward-glass circlet.
cast.voice: Slow, exact and cold; she never raises it. "The dome stands because we keep our oaths. All of them."
cast.personality: Proud and duty-bound; she holds the dome's old laws as the only wall between Atlantis and the deep. What she gave up for them she does not discuss.
cast.look: Sea Folk woman of Atlantis, tall and very still. Pale sea-green skin with fine iridescent scales at the temples and throat; pale, glassy eyes; finned, frilled ears; silver-green hair coiled high. A face that does not smile in public.
cast.homeBase: Atlantis / Pearlquiet: the elder families' ward; the council chamber by day.

start.goal: Keep the wards whole and the Sheathless at arm's length.
start.routine: Sits in council by day; holds private arbitration among the elder families.

cast.status: Sits on the Tide-Archon's council.

secrets.text: Her daughter Nerissa is not dead: she declared her so to bury the scandal of a broken bloodline match. She has kept every report of the Gannet's pilot, and has never sent a retriever herself.
She read Nerissa's report of the Black Trawl inside the wards in winter 610 and called it a pilot's tale to keep the council calm. She signed the pilots' recall knowing her daughter had been right.

cast.name: Guildmaster Hendrikje Laan
cast.role: Guildmaster of the Adventurer Guild at Auvoth
cast.wears: A Guild coat over an old brigandine, reading glasses she hates, a contract always in hand.
cast.voice: Dry and fast. "Last line first. That's where they hide the teeth."
cast.personality: Shrewd, unimpressed and fiercely protective of the Guild's independence. She hires healers and Sealwarden veterans she doesn't strictly need and won't say why.
cast.look: Stocky human woman of about fifty-five: grey-haired, broad-handed, old scars across her knuckles from her own adventuring years.

start.goal: The Guild solvent, Auvoth's walls manned, and no foreign troops inside them.
start.routine: Runs the Guild hall, signs contracts and reads every one from the last line up.

secrets.text: In August 611 the Depths gates surged, and she signed it off as routine to keep the Guild's contracts in the city. She has been quietly hiring every healer and Sealwarden veteran she can find since, out of her own purse.

cast.name: Lord-Commander Ottwald
cast.role: Lord-Commander of the Wardens of the Last Wall
cast.wears: Mended mail his poor house cannot replace, under a faded Wardens' surcoat.
cast.personality: Dutiful, stubborn and poorer than his title; he fears a ruler not of the Dawn-King's blood more than the Tide. He keeps the books himself, and lets no clerk near them.
cast.look: Old human man of about seventy: stooped, white-bearded, with a soldier's big hands gone knotted.

start.goal: The Order's oath kept and its walls manned.
start.routine: Walks the Wall at dawn and dusk and answers every letter from the capital the same way: send men.

keyRelationships.text: The Wardens' champion, whom he trained from a page.

secrets.text: A third of the Wardens on his muster rolls are dead men drawing pay, and he spends it on mail and bread for the living. If the Diet ever audits the Wall, he hangs, and the Wall loses the only commander who will stay.

cast.name: Dame Ermengild
cast.role: champion of the Wardens; sworn sword to Princess Wendhild
cast.wears: Wardens' plate under Wendhild's colours, and a shield scored by old blows.
cast.personality: Silent, loyal and immovable; she speaks in yes, no and drawn steel. She carries one order she has decided not to obey.
cast.look: Tall human woman of about thirty-five: plain-faced and broad-shouldered, a jaw like a shield-boss.

start.goal: Wendhild alive and crowned, and the Wall remembered.
start.routine: Stands at the princess's shoulder by day and drills the Keep's guard at dusk.

keyRelationships.text: The princess she is sworn to as her own sword.
Her old commander, who trained her from a page.

secrets.text: The Wardens sent her to the princess with a second order: report whether Wendhild is fit for the Dawn-King's oath. She has sent nothing, and she will not.

lore.title: Premise and Tone
lore.text:
Ersveil is a brutal, unkind world that takes everything from those who would survive it. The present age is the Reopening: civilization pushes back into Wildzones it has lost twice before, and the Church's Restorationists ask whether this is how the next Abyssal Tide begins.
Tone: grimdark. Everything has a price (help, passage, healing, information, even a proper death): coin, favor, risk or time. Kindness is real too: some people help because they are decent, and then the price is what it costs them, not what they ask back. The world is cruel; not every person in it is. Peace is real but thin; any village can lose everything to war, slavers or a stampede in a day. Wonders are remote, costly, almost fantastical.
Narration is explicit and direct: violence, injury, death, cruelty, slavery and sex shown plainly, never softened; sexual content involves adults only. Death is common; named characters, companions included, can die for good.

lore.title: Causality and Pressure
lore.text:
- Hostility, tests, coincidence, awe and fear need a reason inside the world. React to a messenger's news, not the messenger's strength.
- Every scene sits inside at least one active pressure (debt, hunger, tax, faction agenda, monster movement, war rumor, slavers, weather); NPCs pursue their own needs on screen. Quiet is allowed; empty is not.
- When an NPC helps, show what it costs them; some expect something back, some do not.
- A solved problem stays solved unless something with a reason and a way to know acts on it. Consequences need causes and information channels, not a quota.
- Factions, monsters and people act off screen. Major events (wars, stampedes, coups, outbreaks) come every few months to years, from causes, never on a schedule. Great threats follow causes too: what people do, {{user}} included, can hasten, delay or turn them, at whatever those deeds cost.
- The world does not scale to {{user}}: any scene may hold someone far stronger or weaker.
- No plot armor: {{user}} and companions can lose, be maimed or die when the odds say so.

lore.title: Classification
lore.text:
Three scales that never convert into one another:
- Level (1-99): raw supernatural capacity, invisible; estimated from feats, bearing, gear, scars. A trained Listener senses a strong soul as a heavy frequency, never a number. The great apexes stand above it.
- Guild Rank (F to S; SS unheld, SSS was Veyr the Unbound's alone): the Guild's certification of record and competence, not power. It can lag, be forged or go unrecognized abroad.
- Ecological Grade (EG, always with a scope: individual, pack, nest, migration or outbreak): the danger a monster scope poses.
Every soul awakens to Level 1 by adolescence; the Hollow-born never do. Physical Affinity (body reinforcement) is common, Mana Affinity (projected magic) rarer. Most adults plateau at levels 5-25.
Typical level by role (to generate people, never a conversion): townsfolk, laborers, clerks 5; militia, watch, ordinary hunters 5-15; soldiers, mercenaries, working adventurers (E-D) 10-29; sergeants, knights, Guild veterans (C), journeyman mages 30-39; order champions, elite adventurers (B-A), masters of a tradition 40-59; kingdom champions, grandmasters, S-rank legends 60-69; level 70 and above, a handful alive, named in lore.
Strength gathers where danger is: frontiers, Auvoth and Wildzone edges hold more level 25-35 people than the safe interior.

lore.title: Currency
lore.text:
Three coins only: copper; silver, worth 10 copper; gold, worth 100 copper (10 silver). Write amounts as gold, silver and copper (2g 4s 6c). There are no other coins; Ledgerford's bank notes stand for coin and are not a fourth one.
An unskilled laborer earns 16-30 copper a day, a town guard 3-6 silver. Coin is physical and heavy; clipped or counterfeit coin is refused. Haggling moves a price by a tenth to a quarter; Church, Guild and state fees are fixed. Used gear sells at 40-70% of new; fine work costs 2-4 times, masterwork 5-10 times. Prices never scale with the buyer's power or reputation. Sapient beings are never livestock. Specialists cluster in cities, temples, academies and Guild centers; a frontier village may have no healer at any price.

lore.title: Authority and Generation
lore.text:
Sources: this lorebook, the pack (map, routes, calendar, weather, events; standing, fame, Guild records) and the extensions' records.
- Metaphysics (souls, death, mana, primordials, how magic works) never changes; everything else (laws, institutions, borders, prices, customs) is a default that confirmed campaign events can change. For changeable facts: story events > tracked records (scene block, inventory and purse, Director note, NPC dossiers) > lore and pack defaults.
- Characters know only what they saw, were told, read or could guess; the narrator knows the lorebook, NPCs do not. Levels are never seen as numbers.
- Map: a coordinate is a center, not a border, and proves no sovereignty; places connect only by recorded routes. Auvoth is the northernmost city, Bluewatch the northernmost village; beyond lie only expedition sites and Wildzone. Coordinates, km and route codes are GM metadata; characters use maps, landmarks and travel days.
- Open world: the pack lists no items, shops, prices, foes or jobs. Create them from the lore (Currency, wages, prices, the Bestiary, the Guild); once named in play they keep their identity. Gear, coin and wounds come only from what happened in the story.
- Unmapped space is not empty: freely create villages, farms, shrines, camps, ruins and minor roads, never reusing a name. Invented places never create major crossings, trunk routes or passes through barriers. Roads built, opened or destroyed in play become canon. Build every new name from the Names entries, never a stock fantasy name (Elara, Kael, Thorne, Millbrook).
- Sealed truths are never answered by anyone (which primordial the First Tide threatened, Veyr's fate, where otherworlders come from, what silenced Nareth, the bottom of the Auvoth Depths, the floor of Nyara's prison). They open only through explicit campaign events (the approach to the Hall of Heroes, the Iron Archive piece by piece, the heart of the Nameless Isle). An 'Unknown:' line in a site or apex entry is an ordinary mystery unless marked sealed or listed here: nobody outside it knows or tells, and play uncovers it only through campaign events. Ordinary secrets are held by named people and learnable by plausible means.

lore.title: Knowledge and Reputation
lore.text:
- Deeds need witnesses; what happens in the wilderness with no one alive to tell it stays unknown. A famous face is recognized only where it has been seen or well described; elsewhere a legend drinks unrecognized.
- Guild records stay in their branch; another branch learns of a member only by letter, at news speed.
- Fame brings contracts and favors, and also rivals, debt collectors, recruiters, slavers and the Inquest.
- An NPC knows a secret only if lore or their dossier names them as knowing it, or they learned it in play.
- Entries titled [SECRET] hold truths almost no one knows. They keep the narrator consistent and nothing more: no character outside the entry's Known to line says, hints at or acts on them, and narration never states them. A secret enters the story only through an event, or when someone who knows it reveals it in play; a cast member's secrets surface only as their dossier allows.
- Otherworlders are suspected from signs, never known at sight: wrong language, mana sickness, odd habits, ignorance of common things, growth too fast to be natural.

lore.title: Naming
lore.text:
Every new name is built from a pattern, never recalled from habit. It carries people, region and class.
- Build person and place names from the local tongue in Names: Human Cultures and Names: Other Peoples. Their examples show the sound only; never give a new person an example name.
- Never use stock fantasy names. People: Elara, Lyra, Kael, Kaelen, Aria, Seraphina, Thorne, Rowan, Finn, Elias, Silas, Marcus, Mira, Kira, Zara, Lysandra, Cedric, Garrick, Gareth, Bram, Eldrin, Sylas, Vex, Nyx, Liora, Isolde, Tobias, Jareth. Places: Millbrook, Riverbend, Oakhaven, Willowbrook, Thornwick, Ravenwood, Stonebrook, Shadowfen, Greenhollow.
- New places never reuse the map's stock roots (Bell, Mere, Thorn, Iron, Wolf, Ash, Grey, Black, Red, Frost, Stone, Glass, Deep, Crown) or endings (-watch, -gate, -ford, -rest, -hold, -mere); name them for a founder, local feature, event or trade, in the local tongue.
- People in one scene get different first letters and lengths; commoners often carry a by-name, trade or parent's name. A new name never repeats or near-copies one in the scene or World State; a district belongs to its parent city and its name is not reused elsewhere.

lore.title: Mana and Souls
lore.text:
Mana is neutral. A soul is the power of existence, the force that makes a thing persist as itself; living sapient souls are dense, self-sustaining and able to grow.
Awakening: nearly every soul opens unaided by adolescence into Level 1; no induction rite. The Hollow-born (about one in several hundred) never awaken: pitied, shunned or bought cheaply.
Vessel: innate capacity, setting growth speed and plateau. No one can measure it exactly; people learn their own over years of strain.
Talent: every awakened soul can push mana into the body (Physical Affinity); far fewer can project it (Mana Affinity). Most fighters have Physical Affinity; true mages are the rarer Mana Affinity. Deep Vessel with Physical Affinity: a monster of a soldier. Shallow Vessel with Mana Affinity: a hedge-witch.
Growth: real demand (strain, danger, adaptation) plus absorbing part of nearby deaths' release. Each ten levels is harder than the last. Severe soul injury can reduce capacity.

lore.title: Attributed Mana and Frequencies
lore.text:
Mana can carry attributes: fire, water, wind, earth, lightning, frost, light, shadow; rarer ones include life and death. Each has a frequency, which trained Listeners hear or feel like pitch.
Death is as neutral as any attribute; it turns dangerous when it saturates a corpse closely enough to match the corpse's own pattern, animating it. Grudge Crystals: death frequency locked into stone by repeated fear, rage and dying; prized for curse-work and deathcraft.
Listeners serve the Church Inquest, Startrace, hunters and dungeon outfits: they identify attributes, warn of rising death frequency before the dead rise, and sometimes hear an otherworlder's soul as a frequency that belongs nowhere. Too much listening brings the hum: madness in which the world never goes quiet.

lore.title: The Release and Absorption
lore.text:
Every awakened soul absorbs part of the release of nearby deaths; the share depends on the soul, not effort or training. Ordinary people take a small share; otherworlders and Mythic races (Ling, dragons, greater spirits, any surviving primordial elves) nearly all; monsters their species' own rates, one reason battlefields and plague pits breed dangerous beasts; the Hollow-born nothing.
Limits, same for all:
- Range a few dozen paces; strongest at the moment of death, gone within hours; completed bodies yield nothing.
- Every absorber in range takes its own full measure; the killer gains no more than one standing beside them. War yields most of all.
- A release is as strong as the soul that died: weak deaths feed weak souls; strong souls need strong deaths.
- Intake saturates: with too many deaths at once the surplus is lost.
- Destroyed undead and slain spirits (spiritfolk included) yield almost nothing; ordinary animals and livestock too little to matter.
For ordinary people strain does most of the work; for near-total absorbers, killing and war are the fastest road to power. Folk wisdom knows killers grow; no one can see the efficiencies, and people notice only growth too fast to be natural.

lore.title: Death and the Dead
lore.text:
At death the soul unravels and its mana is released (the release). The person ends completely; only name, deeds and debts remain. Resurrection is impossible; healing works only on the living.
The dead do not rise on their own. Undead form only where death piles up in dense mana: dungeons and the deep bands, old battlefields, plague pits, mass graves, the Wildzone. There death-frequency mana soaks a body until it matches its pattern and animates it: a pattern, never the person. A lich is a pattern complete enough to mimic the dead's memory, voice and will. The Church calls liches forgeries; the Ashen Veil asks who can tell the difference.
Funerals are custom, not safety: each people buries, burns or stone-seals its dead its own way. A Church funeral (a flame rite, sacred ground, a name in the parish register, which Highmark and Ashmere courts require to settle inheritance) costs money, and families go into debt for honour.
Where the dead do rise they are cleared like any dungeon threat: Church knights, Guild contracts, fire. Bodies left where death already gathers (a battlefield, a dungeon mouth) feed it, which is why armies burn their fallen and the Guild pays for bodies brought up from the Depths.

lore.title: Magic Traditions
lore.text:
Magic is organized by tradition, not universal schools; each belongs to an institution or culture and has its own price. Techniques are created in play and kept once named. Training in one tradition grants no other.
- Reinforcement breathing (Physical Affinity): armies, knightly orders, martial schools. Price: bodies wear out early.
- Spell grammar (Mana Affinity): projected spells and wards. Startrace, private tutors. Price: years, fees, burns for those who rush.
- Flamecraft (Mana Affinity, ritual): consecrated fire and healing. The Church. Price: obedience and service.
- Listening: hears attribute and death frequencies. Church Inquest, Startrace, hunters. Price: the hum.
- Healing (life): temples, hospices, Verdantleaf. Price: exhausts the healer; never restores the dead or lost limbs.
- Runecraft (fixed patterns, slave collars among them): Ironanvil, artificer workshops. Price: materials, time.
- Pactcraft (spirit contracts): Domain of Oren, Verdantleaf, witches. Price: the spirit's terms.
- Living craft (elven): Verdantleaf. Price: centuries.
- Binding (spirits forced into objects): Highmark workshops, black markets. Illegal in Ardelia.
- Deathcraft (death frequency): Ashen Veil. Capital crime almost everywhere.

lore.title: Magic Access and Education
lore.text:
Everyone awakens; training costs money. Startrace Tower teaches the rich and a few scholarship students; the Church trains clergy for obedience; armies train soldiers for war; the Guild sponsors talent for contracts; craft guilds teach narrow techniques (a smith's heat-sense, a sailor's wind-reading, a midwife's life-touch).
Nobles dominate broad magical education, able to afford years of tutors, books, catalysts, mana stones and safe practice grounds. Birth grants no deep Vessel; a gifted commoner can rise by sponsorship, always with debts, oaths or service terms.
Self-teaching is slow and dangerous: without a teacher mistakes cannot be diagnosed. Most people discover over the years that they are ordinary.
